items.quote: The bridge is built to a design by William Henry Barlow and John Hawkshaw, based on an earlier design by Isambard Kingdom Brunel
items.note: Two problems. (a) Wikipedia's lead says the bridge as built is Barlow and Hawkshaw's design based on Brunel's; Brunel died in 1859 and it was completed in 1864, so a pedant can argue. (b) Q2 opens 'Which Brunel steamship', which gives this answer away if a team hears Q2 before handing in. Reword Q1: 'Whose winning design of 1831 was the basis for the Clifton Suspension Bridge, finished after his death?' and Q2: 'Which steamship, launched in 1843, is now a museum in a Bristol dry dock?' (still unique: SS Great Britain).

items.quote: Now listed as part of the National Historic Fleet, Great Britain is a visitor attraction and museum
items.note: Launched (floated out) 19 July 1843. See Q1 for the giveaway in this question's 'Brunel' wording.

items.quote: Park also developed the clay modelled shorts featuring the adventures of Wallace & Gromit

items.quote: Teams from the UK and other parts of the world bring their hot air balloons to the site and participate in mass ascents where as many as 100 balloons may launch at a time
items.note: Answer is right and unique, but 'hundreds of hot-air balloons lift off' overstates it: Wikipedia says as many as 100 launch at a time, and the organisers bill 'over 100 balloons'. A host will get corrected by a local. Reword: 'Every August, more than a hundred hot-air balloons lift off from Ashton Court for which event?'
